newsitem.title: UK: Britain calls Bosnia peace implementation meeting.
newsitem.headline: Britain calls Bosnia peace implementation meeting.

text.p: Britain said on Thursday it will host an international conference in December to decide how to consolidate peace in Bosnia next year.
A statement from the Foreign Office said the December 4-5 meeting will be attended by some 50 countries and international agencies as well as by newly-elected Bosnian leaders.
"The London conference will take decisions on the various threads of international civilian involvement in Bosnia next year," it added.

But the conference will not decide on any future military presence in Bosnia after the current NATO-led peace implementation force (IFOR) leaves on December 20, it said, adding this is a matter for NATO's North Atlantic Council.
Britain convened a similar conference in December last year.

It hammered out a framework for returning the former Yugoslav province to some kind of normality after a bloody civil war, via a Peace Implementation Council consisting of 42 states and 10 international organisations.
The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) was charged with organising elections, monitoring human rights and encouraging demilitarisation.
